# Squash migrations to one baseline per module

**Source:** MAG-83 — https://linear.app/magus-monitor/issue/MAG-83/squash-migrations-to-one-baseline-per-module-each-with-its-own-goose
**Generated by:** kkpa-pickup-linear-ticket (PICKUP mode, pipeline declined by the owner)
**Originating prompt:** "MAG-83 Que piensas de ese ticket? Ya todo main esta deployed en PROD. Creo que la idea es eliminar los existentes migraciones, y regenerar un archivo de migracion con la estructura actual de BD, es eso cierto?"
**Unit tests:** excluded

## Why

The four module migration folders share one `public.goose_db_version` table. Two
modules cannot use the same version number: goose records the number once and
silently skips the second file, reporting success. This already happened —
`charging/20260720000001_require_location_kind.sql` has never run in any database,
because `account/20260720000001_vehicles_add_access_type.sql` takes the number
first. Measured on prod on 2026-09-17: 54 applied versions against 55 files on disk.

Migrations are applied one folder at a time, so a later module's migration can read
an earlier module's table. Four migrations do exactly that. It works only because
the dependency direction happens to match the folder order, and it breaks the moment
the earlier module changes that table. MAG-65 hit this and gave up: it could not drop
`telemetry.vehicle_snapshots.account_id`, because `analytics/20260908000002` joins
that column on every fresh database. The column is still there, nullable and unwritten.

`make migration-guard` exists only to hold the collision back. It carries a list of
known duplicates. `goose.WithAllowOutofOrder(true)` is on repo-wide for the same
reason, which disables goose's own protection against a migration arriving late.

One baseline per module removes all of it by construction. One file per folder has no
order to get wrong, and a baseline creates tables without reading anything, so the
cross-module SQL disappears instead of being re-ordered around.

## What Changes

- Replace the 55 migration files under `internal/{account,telemetry,charging,analytics}/db/migrations/`
  with **one baseline file per module**, holding that module's schema as it stands today.
- All four baselines carry the **same version number**, `20260917000001`. This was
  impossible before and is legal now, and it proves in the repo that the collision class is gone.
- Each baseline's `-- +goose Down` **raises an exception** naming the reason. It is not
  empty and it does not drop the schema. **BREAKING** for `make migrate-down`: the
  command now fails on a baseline instead of walking past it.
- Give each module **its own goose version table** — `<module>.goose_db_version`, inside
  the Postgres schema that module already owns — through `goose.WithTableName`.
- Add **one normal migration after the baselines** that drops
  `telemetry.vehicle_snapshots.account_id`. This is the single deliberate schema change.
- **Remove** `make migration-guard` and `KNOWN_DUPLICATE_MIGRATIONS`. Collisions become
  impossible, and a deleted guard beats a maintained one.
- **Turn off** `goose.WithAllowOutofOrder(true)` in `cmd/migrate/main.go` and
  `internal/testdb/testdb.go`, restoring goose's late-migration protection.
- Add a **new guard** that fails when a migration references another module's Postgres
  schema. This is the root cause, and without the guard the problem returns with the
  next cross-module backfill.
- Stamp dev and prod: create their four version tables and seed the baseline version,
  so the baselines never run against a database that already has the tables.

Out of scope, waived by the owner: `charging.manual_charge_entries.location_kind`
nullability. No row is NULL today, and the Go insert path never writes NULL.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `schema-migrations`: how the platform's database schema migrations are organised,
  numbered, recorded and bounded — one self-contained baseline per module, a version
  ledger private to each module, and the rule that a migration may only touch its own
  module's schema.

### Modified Capabilities

None. The `platform` capability's migration requirements stay true: the one-shot
migration step still runs after a healthy database and still must succeed before the
gateway and poller start. The `telemetry` capability never required
`vehicle_snapshots.account_id` — it requires the account id on `poll_attempts`, which
is `polled_by_account_id` and is untouched.

## Impact

**Migrations** — 55 files deleted, 5 created (4 baselines + 1 drop-column migration).

**Code** — `cmd/migrate/main.go` and `internal/testdb/testdb.go`: add `WithTableName`
per module, remove `WithAllowOutofOrder`.

**Build** — `Makefile`: delete `migration-guard` and `KNOWN_DUPLICATE_MIGRATIONS`, add
the cross-module-schema guard, update `check`. `deploy/docker/Dockerfile`'s four `COPY`
lines keep working unchanged, because the folder paths do not move.

**Codegen** — `sqlc.yaml` needs no change: `schema:` already points at each module's
migrations folder. Re-run `sqlc generate`; the only expected `models.go` diff is the
dropped `AccountID` field on the telemetry snapshot model.

**Databases** — dev and prod both need their four version tables created and seeded.
This is the one risky step. goose v3.27.3 has no `stamp` or `force` command, so it is
hand-written SQL. Every database command in this change is run by the owner, never by
an assistant.

**Deploy order** — the stamp MUST land on prod before the deploy that carries the
baselines. `web` and `poller` declare `depends_on: migrate: condition:
service_completed_successfully`, so a failing migrate step keeps both from starting.

**Docs** — `README.md`, `ai/architecture.md`, `ai/go-conventions.md`, `cmd/README.md`,
the four modules' `AGENTS.md`, and `kkpa/context/architecture/schema-per-module.md`.

**Accepted cost** — replayable migration history is lost. `git log` keeps every file,
and `public.goose_db_version` is left in place as the record of what was applied and
when.
